solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Notice that one has expired old coin

parts.note: a bit is an old coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: Someone spots that their old coin has passed out of use and is no longer legal tender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice that one has expired' looks like it describes the coin going out of circulation, but it defines a death notice.
explanation.definitionFit: An obit is short for obituary, a newspaper announcement of a person's death.

clue.text: Spanish robber's a born criminal claiming benefits

indicators.note: claiming means the rearranged letters take in the word for benefits
criminal suggests the letters of a born are bent out of their order

parts.note: the dole is British slang for state unemployment benefits

explanation.surface: A born crook from Spain is caught fiddling welfare payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' turns A BORN into BANRO, which 'claiming' wraps round DOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandolero is a Spanish bandit or highwayman.

clue.text: Come to drink, beer for the most part

parts.note: a tot is a small drink of spirits

indicators.note: for the most part means most of the beer word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: ale is beer

explanation.surface: Someone is invited round for a drink, mostly beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops the last letter of ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To total is to add up to, as in 'the bill came to ten pounds'.

clue.text: School having no particular assembly

parts.note: a comp is a comprehensive school, the standard British state secondary school
any means no particular one, as in 'pick any'

explanation.surface: A school that holds no special morning gathering of pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: COMP is British slang for a comprehensive, the non-selective state secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: A company is a gathering of people, as in 'in good company', so it can mean an assembly.

clue.text: Hardly any toast Conservative, defeat ahead

parts.note: a rout is a heavy defeat
on means ahead, as in 'getting on'

explanation.surface: Hardly anyone toasts the Tory party, which faces defeat ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a small cube of fried or toasted bread, so only a tiny scrap of toast.

clue.text: Expert at Morse codes

indicators.note: codes suggests the letters of at Morse are encrypted, scrambled into another form

explanation.surface: Someone is skilled at sending Morse messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'codes' looks like a noun about Morse, but it is the verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a master of an art, especially a distinguished musician.

clue.text: In this fashion sat on top of roan to go off?

definitions.text: In this fashion sat on top of roan to go off?

indicators.note: in a down clue, sat on top of roan places the reshaped letters above the horse's letter
fashion is a verb here, meaning shape the letters of sat into a new form
top of means the first letter of roan

parts.note: to addle is to go off or turn rotten, as an egg does

explanation.surface: A rider mounted on a roan horse asks how to set off.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue pictures the position itself: a rider sitting over a roan's back, about to ride away, which is the only fashion of sitting the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: Astraddle means with a leg on either side, the way a rider sits on a horse.

clue.text: I agree skirts are short, showing age

indicators.note: skirts means the word for agreement goes round the other piece

parts.note: yes means I agree

indicators.note: short means the word are loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An older person approves of short skirts, which reveal their age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts ARE to AR, which YES 'skirts'. 'showing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Years is a synonym of age, as in 'a man of his years'.

clue.text: Nick raised tailless domestic fowl

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, means the word for nick is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to nab is to nick, or catch

indicators.note: tailless means the word for domestic loses its last letter

parts.note: tame means domestic, not wild

explanation.surface: Someone stole a farmyard bird and raised it to be tame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns NAB into BAN; 'tailless' cuts TAME to TAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of domestic chicken.

clue.text: 7 of 13

parts.note: read as the YEARS (7 down) of STEPHEN SONDHEIM (13 across), the age at which the composer died in November 2021; it is also seven times thirteen

explanation.surface: A bare cross-reference that looks like a fraction or a multiplication.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer at 7 is YEARS and the one at 13 is STEPHEN SONDHEIM, who died aged ninety-one shortly before this puzzle ran; seven times thirteen gives the same number.
explanation.definitionFit: Sondheim's age at death, and the product of the two numbers, are both this figure.

clue.text: Those voting against retaining shillings and inches

indicators.note: retaining means the word for those against holds the letter inside

parts.note: the noes are those voting against a motion
S is an abbreviation for shillings, the old British coin

explanation.surface: Opponents of a motion on the old money and imperial units keep both.
explanation.walkthrough: S for shillings comes from the pre-decimal British currency. 'and' is a link word; 'inches' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose is to edge forward slowly, as a car noses into traffic, so it means inch along.

clue.text: Accessory for princess regularly taking trip abroad

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words trip abroad, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A princess packs a piece of finery for an overseas trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled crown-like headpiece, the classic adornment worn by a princess.

clue.text: See writing brilliantly presented on the stage

parts.note: to spot is to see
lit, short for literature, means writing

explanation.surface: A theatregoer is told to watch a play script performed superbly.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who is spotlit stands in the bright beam of a stage lamp.

clue.text: Fresh rains during dry crossing

indicators.note: during says the reworked letters come inside the abstinence abbreviation

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means dry in the sense of not drinking

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters of rains made new, in a different order

explanation.surface: New showers fall in the middle of a drought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' looks like the opposite of rain; here it means teetotal, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A transit is a passage or journey across something, so a crossing.

clue.text: Composer of Rocket Man? He has stupid clothing

parts.note: George Stephenson built the Rocket locomotive, so he is the Rocket man

indicators.note: clothing means the word for stupid wraps round the two letters of He

parts.note: dim means stupid

explanation.surface: It looks like it asks who wrote 'Rocket Man', and adds that he wears daft clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer of Rocket Man' looks like Elton John; 'Composer' alone is the definition, and Rocket is the steam engine George Stephenson built in 1829.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Sondheim was the American who wrote the music and lyrics for Company and Sweeney Todd.

clue.text: Busy at Chinese, making reservation

indicators.note: busy suggests the letters of at Chinese are bustling about into a new order

explanation.surface: A packed Chinese restaurant means one has to book a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reservation' looks like a table booking; it is doubt. 'making' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitance is a holding back from doubt, the same as having reservations.

clue.text: Rough area of housing to bury one's diamonds

indicators.note: to bury means the housing word takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: an estate is an area of housing
I'm is a contraction of one is, I being one
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: In a rough neighbourhood someone buries their diamonds for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' looks like it describes the area, but it is the definition, as in a rough guess.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimated figure is an approximate one, a rough guess.

clue.text: Guy in today's paper with news on mad dog

indicators.note: in an across clue, news on mad means the news word follows the mad word

parts.note: cross means mad in the sense of angry
word means news, as in 'send word'
a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A man in the newspaper reports on a rabid dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like any man, but it is this puzzle's setter, whose pseudonym is Guy.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy is the pen name of the compiler who wrote this very puzzle for the newspaper.

clue.text: A selection of musical icon's material

indicators.note: A selection of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sample of fabric from a famous Broadway star's wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain cotton cloth, a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Hurry after deliveries take longer than expected

indicators.note: after means the hurry word comes below the deliveries word

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
to run is to hurry

explanation.surface: Couriers rush around once parcels are delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is a set of six deliveries (balls) bowled from one end in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to go past the time allotted, as a meeting does.

clue.text: Woman specially fitted to dry Oscar Hammerstein's head

indicators.note: specially fitted suggests the letters are reassembled to make something new

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: head means the first letter of Hammerstein's

explanation.surface: A dryer is custom-installed for a lyricist's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially fitted' mixes TODRY, O and H. Oscar Hammerstein wrote lyrics for Rodgers and was Sondheim's mentor.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Perceptive faculty performing college roles at first

parts.note: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school

indicators.note: at first means the first letter of roles

explanation.surface: A drama school's staff are casting the first parts.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is London's best-known drama school.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar is used figuratively for an instinctive ability to notice things, as in 'on my radar'.

clue.text: Song that shouldn't be rearranged

definitions.meaning: to let something be is to leave it as it is, not alter it

explanation.surface: A song so perfect that nobody should tinker with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearranged' looks like an anagram signal, but no letters here make the answer: it is a second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Beatles hit whose title phrase means 'leave it alone', i.e. don't change it.

clue.text: Drunk turned up to host New York awards

indicators.note: to host means the reversed word holds the other letters inside
turned up, in a down clue, means the drunkard word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a sot is a drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk arrives to present a New York ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' turns SOT into TOS, which then holds NY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tonys are the annual Broadway theatre awards, held in New York.

clue.text: New Yorker's CV director picked up again

parts.note: resume is the American word for a CV

explanation.surface: A director from New York hands in a curriculum vitae.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to continue after a break, so to take something up once more.

clue.text: Insufficient examination ending in oversight

parts.note: a scan is a medical examination

indicators.note: ending in means the last letter of oversight

explanation.surface: A medical check-up ends in a mistake being missed, through not being thorough enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely enough, as in 'scant regard'.

clue.text: Clergyman is a hundred soon

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A priest is about to turn a hundred years old.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a priest attached to a cathedral chapter.

clue.text: Retired player on runs builds muscle

indicators.note: in an across clue, player on runs puts the player word after the runs letter

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
an actor is a player on the stage

explanation.surface: A retired cricketer keeps fit by building up his muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'builds' is a link word; 'muscle' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A retractor is a muscle that draws a body part back in, or a surgical tool that holds tissue apart.

clue.text: New England Yankee clipped by charming eccentric hairdresser

indicators.note: clipped by means the charming word grips the three letters, holding them inside

parts.note: sweet means charming
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
odd means eccentric

explanation.surface: A quirky New England barber with a charming manner gives an American a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipped' suits a haircut but signals that SWEET holds NEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeney Todd, the demon barber of Fleet Street, is the title character of Sondheim's musical, a murderous barber.
